sentences.text: A single-site feasibility trial in a French outpatient chemotherapy clinic examined virtual reality use among adult women with breast cancer who lacked brain metastases or contraindications.
Nurses offered virtual reality sessions during four consecutive chemotherapy appointments, making 217 sessions available to 60 women with a median age of 51.
Approximately 63% of participants used the headset for at least three visits, reporting low simulator sickness, high satisfaction, and a 91% willingness to repeat the experience.
Conversely, nurses expressed less desire to adopt the technology regularly due to the increased workload it imposed.
The authors conclude that further clinical trials are necessary to determine how virtual reality affects patient well-being during treatment.
